I am seventy-one years old. I have worked these same 3 mu for fifty years. I finished primary school, so I can read the numbers on the fertilizer bag and do the sums in my head. My son is off working in Shijiazhou, so it is just me and my wife in the field now. We have a well, and I pump the water myself with my diesel engine.

For the wheat, I will do rotary tillage after the maize comes off in early October. Last year I put one bag of compound fertilizer per 2 mu at sowing — that is 100 jin per mu. The bag says 18-22-5. I get it from the dealer in town. That gives me about 9 kg of nitrogen, 11 kg of phosphorus, and 2.5 kg of potassium per mu. Then at green-up time, around Qingming in April, I will spread 50 jin of urea per mu. Urea is 46 percent nitrogen, so that is another 11.5 kg of nitrogen. All together that is about 20 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. I know Old Wang down the lane puts more, but last year I got 1000 jin per mu — that is 500 kg — and my wheat did not fall over in the wind like his did.

I will irrigate the wheat three times. First, before winter sets in, I flood the field so the wheat roots do not freeze dry. Second, at jointing in April, when the stems shoot up fast. Third, at heading in May, when the grain is filling. If the spring is very dry, maybe I add one more, but three times is what I usually do.

For spraying, I do herbicide once right after sowing to kill the weeds before they come up. Then in spring I spray once for aphids. At heading I spray fungicide once for rust. That is three times total with my backpack sprayer.

For the maize, I plant right after the wheat harvest in early June. I use no-tillage — I just open a shallow furrow and drop the seed. Everyone around here uses hybrid maize now. I buy Nongda or Denghai seed, about 1.5 jin per mu. At planting I put 100 jin per mu of compound fertilizer, the 28-6-6 kind. That gives me about 14 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. Last year I did not even top-dress with urea, and I still got 1100 jin per mu — 550 kg. The leaves stayed green all season.

I irrigate the maize twice: once when the plants have about seven leaves, and again at tasseling. If the summer rains are good, maybe I skip the second one, but I plan for two.

For maize pesticide, I spray herbicide once after planting. Then I spray insecticide once when the corn borers start — usually around the big trumpet stage. If I see armyworm moths, I spray one more time. Last year I needed three sprays total.

My whole farm is only 3 mu. Every bag of fertilizer costs real money — over 100 yuan a bag now. But I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. If I lose half my yield, my grandson's school fees are in trouble. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost; losing the crop is a disaster. So I watch what my neighbors do, and I stay close to them. Last year was a good year, so this year I will do the same.
